children: Neil Ghai New Delhi: The share of Chinese smartphone brands in the Indian market shrank to 67-68% in the July-September quarter, the lowest in more than eight years, as record-high memory chip prices led them to cut budget models - a segment that traditionally drove their sales. Technology market research firm Omdia estimates the share of Chinese brands at 68% in the last quarter, as against 71% in the previous three-month period and 75% a year ago.

The peak was 80%, recorded in the April-June quarter of 2020. According to Counterpoint Research, Chinese brands had a 67% share this July-September, the lowest since the first quarter of 2019. Experts said companies such as Vivo, Oppo and Xiaomi are cutting down on budget models, the segment most impacted by high memory costs, opening space for domestic players like Lava and Ai+ to capture demand from price-sensitive consumers ahead of Diwali. "What Chinese OEMs (original equipment manufacturers) have been doing over the last four to five quarters is that they've been trying to cut down their specs to manage their costs. Essentially, cost optimisation through spec cuts," Omdia principal analyst Sanyam Chaurasia told ET.

title: Chip Costs Loosen China's Grip on Smartphone Mkt
